entities.name: 2017 Sydney Seaplane crash
entities.label: Place
entities.summary: The 2017 Sydney Seaplanes DHC-2 crash occurred on 31 December 2017 at about 3:15 pm AEDT (UTC+11:00), a de Havilland Canada DHC-2 Beaver configured as a floatplane crashed – less than two minutes after takeoff – into Jerusalem Bay off Cowan Creek, on the northern outskirts of Sydney, Australia. The aircraft, operated by Sydney Seaplanes, was carrying five passengers and a pilot, all of whom were killed in the crash. It was returning diners from Cottage Point Inn restaurant to Rose Bay Water Airport. The ATSB believes it probable that the pilot's performance was adversely affected by carbon monoxide poisoning.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The 2017 Sydney Seaplane crash resulted in the loss of five lives and highlighted concerns about pilot safety and carbon monoxide poisoning. The incident led to increased scrutiny of aviation regulations and safety protocols in Australia.
